title: Holy as Thou, O Lord, Is None
description: Holy as Thou, O Lord, Is None in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 136 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Holiness of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ho-ly as thou, O Lord, is none! Thy ho-li-ness is all thine own; A drop of that un-bound-ed sea Is ours, a drop de-rived from thee.

lines: Holy as thou, O Lord, is none!
Thy holiness is all thine own;
A drop of that unbounded sea
Is ours, a drop derived from thee.
And when thy purity we share,
Holy and pure is God alone.
By all the heavenly hosts adored!
Let all on earth bow down to thee,

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
